Note: The Department of Correctional Services is an equal opportunity employer, and the provisions of the Employment Equity Act shall be taken into consideration during the selection for the enrolment as Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Officers. The Department of Correctional Services is recruiting South Africans to serve as Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Officers. Successful candidates will pursue a career in the department focused on inmate rehabilitation, development, secure detention, and social reintegration. The Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Programme is an Internal Occupational Training Programme and is intended to contribute towards addressing the skills shortage in the Department of Correctional Services and addressing unemployment in South Africa. The programme is based on a legally binding agreement between the employer and the trainee. Applicants will be expected to undergo a physical fitness test and medical examination (including a drug test) as part of the selection process. Please take note that correspondence will only be conducted with the shortlisted candidates. If you have not been contacted within three (3) months of the closing date of the advertisement, please accept that your application is unsuccessful. Please do not call the department to enquire about the progress of your application. Applicants must note that further checks will be conducted once they are shortlisted and that their appointment is subject to positive outcomes on these checks, which include security clearance, security vetting, qualification verification and criminal records verification. Appointment will be provisional, pending the issue of a security clearance. If you cannot get a security clearance, your appointment will be re-considered/possibly terminated. Finger prints may be taken on the day of the interview. All shortlisted candidates shall undertake two pre-entry assessments. One shall be a practical exercise, and the other shall be an integrity (ethical conduct) Assessment. Selection panels shall score both technical exercises as an additional criterion in the interview process. Applications: Applications must be submitted on the Z83 form (Public Service application form) available on the link provided below and must be completed in full. Only a detailed CV should be attached to your application form. Only shortlisted candidates will be required to submit certified copies not older than 6 months of qualifications and other related documents on or before the day of the interview. Please send a complete application for the post you apply for on a pdf format, stating the correct reference for the position you are interested in. Requirement for valid driver’s licence is not applicable to applicants with a disability. The trainee shall be regarded as competent after the successful completion of the workplace learning phase. Any contravention or deviation from the Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Programme agreement during the prescribed period of the learning phases shall be dealt with in accordance with the Correctional Services Act, Skills Development Act Sections 17 and 18, enrolment contract/agreement signed between parties, DCS Policies and procedures and other relevant regulations/legislations. After successful completion of the probation period, and subject to the availability of posts, the Department of Correctional Services reserves the right to upgrade candidates to Centre-Based: 1-1 posts. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advert requirements and responsibilities. It is the sole responsibility of an applicant to ensure that their application reaches DCS before the closing date. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill any of these advertised posts. Note: Appointments under the Correctional Services Act. During phase 2, trainees will continue to receive a Centre Based Auxiliary Support salary and shall be responsible for their own accommodation, meals and transport. Taking into consideration that you must provide your own transport and accommodation during your workplace learning, you are advised to apply for Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Programme enrolment within the Management Area close to where you reside. No transfers of trainees will be made during the programme phases.
responsibilities:
The training programme shall consist of two (2) phases: Phase 1: Instructional Learning Phase.
The Centre Based: Auxiliary Support Programme instructional phase shall be presented for a period of 02 months at the designated training college.
The intensive instructional learning shall include: Knowledge modules, firearm skills development training programme, physical training, self-defence training, and some of the necessary practicals.
During this period the department will provide accommodation, meals and training resources (Learning material, stationery, training equipment and uniform).
The instructional training phase requires the trainee to be strictly accommodated on a full-time basis at the training college.
Phase 2: Workplace Learning Phase.
The workplace learning will take place at the Correctional Centres and Social Reintegration/Community Corrections Offices, and in other external environments such as (Courts, hospitals and workplaces) where our inmates are exposed to, for a period of 10 months.
requirements:
Matric/Grade 12 certificate PLUS a recognised Degree/National Diploma (NQF level 6 qualification) in the following fields: Correctional Management/Correctional and Rehabilitation/Penology and Criminology and Qualifications with majors in Corrections, Penology and Criminology.

Citizenship
Qualifications, and criminal record

about_role:
Capitec is hiring a Decision Scientist, based in Stellenbosch.
We're looking for a Decision Scientist to help us ask better questions of our data - and use the answers to build smarter products, sharper processes and faster decisions at scale.
We sit at the intersection of data, technology and real business impact. This role exists to solve meaningful business problems, shape new products and services, and improve the way we make decisions - by turning complex data into clear, actionable insight while keeping risk firmly in view.
responsibilities:
Build and deploy predictive models that directly influence credit and business decisions affecting millions of clients
Apply machine learning and statistical techniques - from logistic regression to neural networks and random forests - to real-world challenges, not just theoretical problems
Work across cloud environments and large databases to extract, transform and interpret data at significant scale
Translate analysis into recommendations that stakeholders at all levels can act on with confidence
Contribute to best practice in how we develop, monitor and reuse models - helping raise the bar across the team
Collaborate with business partners to understand their needs, shape requirements and deliver solutions that stick
Our team:
We work in a dedicated Decision Science function focused on translating active business data into usable strategic information - informing critical, measurable decisions across credit and risk. Our work doesn't sit in a silo. It feeds directly into products and processes used by millions of South Africans every day, which means what you build here has real, visible consequences.
Why this role is different:
You won't be crunching numbers in isolation. We've built a culture of collaboration, innovation and creativity - one where everyone is always thinking ahead and willing to help one another. Even if you've just joined us, you have immediate access to executive management.
This role gives you:
Broad exposure - across credit, risk, compliance and operations, not just one narrow domain
Real influence - your models and analysis shape decisions at a business-wide level
A team that invests in you - we share knowledge freely and expect you to grow as much as you contribute
requirements:
An Honours degree in Mathematics or Statistics (a Master's degree is preferred)
Hands-on experience building and deploying statistical and machine learning models - including logistic regression, neural networks, support vector machines and random forests
Proven ability to work in cloud environments such as Azure or AWS, and with large relational databases
Proficiency in at least one machine learning language - Python or SAS Viya
Practical knowledge of the financial services or credit environment, including an understanding of relevant regulatory frameworks
Strong analytical and numerical reasoning skills, with sharp attention to detail

Sound judgement, strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work with structure and rigour

Note: Applications must be submitted on a Z83 Form (2021 version), obtainable from http://www.dpsa.gov.za/dpsa2g/vacancies.asp, which must be accompanied with a comprehensive Curriculum Vitae. The post particulars and reference number of the post you are applying for, must be correctly specified on the application form. Please complete a separate application form for each post you wish to apply for. It is the responsibility of the applicants to submit applications timeously to the correct physical address as provided in the advertisement. Please note that applications submitted to an incorrect physical address will not be considered. Late applications will not be accepted or considered. Short-listed candidates will be required to produce originals of their Identity Document (ID), Senior Certificate and all educational qualifications obtained, service certificates from previous employers stating the occupation and motor vehicle driver’s license, before the interview. Qualifications and driver’s licences submitted will be subjected to verification with the relevant institutions. Applicants must have no previous criminal convictions or pending criminal/ departmental cases and shall allow their fingerprints to be taken and background enquiries to be made. Short-listed candidates may be subjected to a full security clearance process before or during any stage of employment. Short-listed candidates will be subjected to a vetting process which will include security screening, fingerprint screening, reference checking and verification of address, where necessary. All short-listed candidates, including the SMS, will be expected to undergo a personal interview and shall undertake two pre-entry assessments, (a) a practical exercise to determine a candidate’s suitability based on the post’s technical and generic requirements, as well as (b) an integrity assessment (ethical conduct) assessment. Selection panels shall score both technical exercises as an additional criterion in the interview process. Short-listed candidates for appointments to certain identified posts will be vetted in terms of the Criminal Law (Sexual Offences and Related Matters) Amendment Act, 2007 (Act No 32 of 2007) and the Children’s Act, 2005 (Act No 38 of 2005). A candidate whose particulars appear in either the National Register for Sex Offenders or Part B of the Child Protection Register, will be disqualified from appointment. Candidates are expected to disclose if he/ she is a respondent in an interim or final protection order in terms of the Domestic Violence Act, 1998 (Act no 116 of 1998) or Protection from Harassment Act, 2011 (Act No 17 of 2011), and may be disqualified from appointment. The Criminal Law (Forensic Procedures) Amendment Act, Act 37 of 2013 requires that all new appointments in the South African Police Service as from 31 January 2015 provide a buccal (inside cheek) sample to determine their forensic DNA profile. The forensic DNA profile derived from the sample will be loaded to the Elimination Index of the National Forensic DNA Database. Appointments will be made in terms of the Public Service Act, 1994 (Act No 103 of 1994) as applicable to the post environment. Persons who retired from the Public Service by taking a severance package, early retirement or medical retirement, as well as persons with previous convictions, are excluded. The South African Police Service is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer and it is the intention to promote representivity in the Public Service through the filling of these posts. Persons whose transfer/ appointment will promote representivity will therefore receive preference. The South African Police Service is under no obligation to fill a post after the advertisement thereof. Correspondence will be conducted with successful candidates only. If you have not been contacted within three (3) months after the closing date of this advertisement, please accept that your application was unsuccessful.

job_title: Head of Department: Department of Community Safety, Roads and Transport
about_role:
The Office of the Premier (Free State) is hiring a Head of Department: Department of Community Safety, Roads and Transport, based in Bloemfontein. This is a contract post, paying R1,885,710 a year.
(5-year employment contract position)

How to apply: applications HOD-CSRT post: Dr. M Phera, Director General, Office of the Premier, Attention: Ms. Ruth Sefali, Room 406, OR Tambo House, St Andrew Street, Bloemfontein, 9301, E-mail: ruth.sefali@fspremier.gov.za
Reference number to quote: HOD- CSRT
Closing date: 07 December 2026 @ 16:00
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
Note: Applications must be submitted on the prescribed Z83 form, obtainable from any Public Service Department. The Z83 form must be completed in full and signed by the applicant. All applications must be accompanied by a comprehensive CV only. Communication from the HR of the department regarding the submission of certified copies of qualifications and other relevant documents will be limited to shortlisted candidates. Applications must be submitted on or before the closing date. E-mailed applications may be submitted, subject to subsequent verification. Applications must be submitted to the address mentioned in the advertisement. All shortlisted candidates, including the SMS, shall undertake two pre-entry assessments. One will be a practical exercise to determine a candidate’s suitability based on the post’s technical and generic requirements and the other must be an integrity (ethical conduct) assessment. Selection panels shall score both technical exercises as an additional criterion in the interview process. All shortlisted candidates for SMS posts will be subjected to a technical exercise and interview. Following the technical exercise and interview, a maximum of three (3) SMS candidates will undergo psychometric assessments to assess cognitive capabilities, behavioural preferences, emotional intelligence, and integrity. The competency assessment will be testing generic managerial competencies using the mandated DPSA SMS competency assessment tools. It is the applicant’s responsibility to have foreign qualifications evaluated by the South African Qualification Authority (SAQA). Applications that do not comply with the abovementioned requirements will not be considered. Shortlisted candidates will be subjected to personnel suitability checks/security clearance. Correspondence will be limited to short-listed candidates only. Applicants are respectfully informed that if no response is received within 4 months of the closing date, they must accept that their application was unsuccessful. The department reserves the right not to fill this position. Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply and preference will be given to the EE Targets. No late or faxed applications will be considered.
responsibilities:
Give strategic direction and monitor the effective and efficient functioning of the department in terms of PSA,1994 (as amended) and the PSR including effective utilization and training of staff, maintenance of discipline, promotion of sound labour relations and public service transformation and reform, the Departments strategic direction, operations and performance, effective HRM, and performance and development of officials, including: Internal Audit: Promote good governance, Corporate Services: Ensure availability of skilled, health and motivated workforce, Financial Management Services: Provide financial administration support, Risk Management: Provide enterprise risk management services, and Minimum Information Security Standard (MISS) and overall accountability for security at the Department.
To function as the Accounting Officer of the Department in terms of Public Finance Management Act and Treasury Regulations, including: Convene departmental budget meetings and provide strategic direction and oversight for the department, and ensure that allocations are in line with objectives of different departmental programs set to provide services as required.
In addition also perform the following administrative responsibilities, including: Ensure the effective implementation of Government Policies in the relevant areas of responsibility of the department mentioned and the Public Service as well as Provincial and National legislation relevant to the Portfolio, Provide the MEC with sufficient information and advice to enable a sound and informed decision, and Ensure development and implementation of a Strategic and Annual Performance Plan for the department in support of the implementation of the priorities and objectives of the department.
Monitor, oversee and assess police service delivery in the Free State.
Promote integrated crime prevention initiatives.
Promote and regulate public transport and road safety.
Ensure road safety, integrated transport system and networks.
Provide Government Motor Transport services.
requirements:
A post graduate qualification (NQF level 8) as recognized by SAQA as well as 10 years of experience at a senior management level.
Potential applicants for posts in the Senior Management Service as well as existing SMS members who will progress to higher levels within the SMS are expected to successfully complete the compulsory preentry Certificate for entry into the SMS which took effect on 1 April 2020 (Full details can be sourced by following the link: http://www.thensg.gov.za/trainingcourse/sms-pre-entry-programme/.
Individual applicants are expected to pay for the course, the duration of the course is 120 hours).
No applicant will be appointed in the absence of the certificate.

Departmental Functions: Form part of the assessment workstreams for Office of the Premier.

Appropriate qualification at NQF Level 7 in Organisational Development/Work study/Management Services/Industrial Psychology field as recognised by the South African Qualification Authority (SAQA) or equivalent.

Knowledge of Organizational Design principles, legislation and processes, Job Evaluation processes, legislation and principles, BPM legislation, principles and legislation, Job Description legislation policies and processes.

about_role:
The Department of Health (Gauteng) is hiring a Head Clinical Department: Medical in Anaesthesia, based in Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital. This is a permanent post, paying R2,704,842 a year.
(Re-advertisement, those who previously applied are encouraged to re-apply) Directorate: Anaesthesia

How to apply: should be submitted strictly online at the following E-Recruitment portal: http://jobs.gauteng.gov.za. No hand-delivered, faxed, or emailed applications will be accepted.
Reference number to quote: REFS/057424
Closing date: 04 December 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
Note: Kindly note that no payment of any kind is required when applying for posts advertised by the Gauteng Department of Health. The Department reserves the right not to fill any advertised posts. Applications should be accompanied by a fully completed and signed new Z83 form obtainable from any Public Service Department or on the internet at www.dpsa.gov.za/documents. The new Z83 form must be fully completed and signed by the applicant. The following must be considered in relation to the completion of the Z83 by applicants: All the fields in Part A, Part C and Part D must be completed. “If your profession or occupation requires official registration, provide date and particulars of registration”. Application without proof of a new Z83 application form and detailed CV will be disqualified. Applicants must indicate the post reference number on their applications. Shortlisted candidates will receive communication from HR unit to submit certified copies of educational qualifications and other relevant documents not older than 6 months on or before the day of the interview. All shortlisted candidates, including SMS, shall undertake two pre-entry assessments. One must be a practical exercise, and the other must be an Integrity (Ethical Conduct) Assessment. Selection panels shall score both technical exercises as an additional criterion in the interview process. Personnel Suitability Checks (criminal checks, citizenship checks, qualification verification, company directorship, social media, financial record checks, reference checks) must be conducted prior appointment. Candidates in possession of a foreign qualification must furnish the Department with an evaluation certificate from the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA). Applicants with foreign qualifications remain responsible for ensuring that their qualifications are evaluated by the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA). The recommended candidate may be subjected to medical surveillance by the Occupational Health and Safety Act, Act 5/1993. The performance of normal and commuted overtime is not mandatory; however, it will be based on the operational needs of the hospitals.
responsibilities:
Co-ordinate, manage and administer efficient and cost-effective anaesthesia services at the institution.
Encourage and foster research within the department.
Manage and monitor appropriate and relevant undergraduate and postgraduate teaching and training within anaesthesia.
Foster appropriate subspecialty development within the department.
Promote staff development and where possible to further the aims of the faculty of sciences and the department of anaesthesia.
Encourage collaboration between the departments within the teaching complex.
Ensure that clinical teaching and supervision of medical staff are of adequate standards.
As part of the university’s responsibility, provide sufficient and quality teaching to undergraduates and medical students.
Set norms and standards for the maintenance of service delivery and quality outputs in the department.
Ensure that the strategic plan and the turnaround strategy of the hospital is implemented and be part of the executive management team in the hospital.
Manage and provide leadership in delivery of clinical services to patients referred to the hospital for anaesthesia problems.
Perform clinical duties in areas of personal special interest and expertise.
See to fit that quality assurance, including clinical audit is conducted in the department in line with national core standards.
Lead the department of anaesthesia of Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital, in line with the strategic goals set by the National and Provincial Departments of Health and the Chief Executive Officer of the hospital.
Participate in the management activities of Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital as a whole and attend all applicable management meetings.
Participate in university academic management activities, including membership of committees in the Faculty of Health Sciences as a whole and in the university’s Department of Anaesthesia.
Lead and participate in national and international efforts to advance aspects of Anaesthesia, both in research and advocacy.
Examine and provide examiners for degree and diploma programmes and fellowships in anaesthesia in other universities and colleges in South Africa.
Ensure that appropriate, ethical and quality research is performed in the department as part of a wider agenda to explore improvements in healthcare in the hospital area and South Africa as a whole, with publication of the results in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
Provide clinical support and outreach to referring hospitals, community health centres and clinics in the Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital health cluster.
Ensure the employment of the previously advantaged individuals in terms of race, gender and disability to enhance equity.
Perform commuted overtime as per departmental requirement.
Contribute to anaesthesia planning, budgeting and procurement processes as well as monitoring and evaluation.
Be immediately accountable in the execution of duties jointly to the Director Clinical Support of Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital and to the Academic Head in the Department of Anaesthesia at the University of Witwatersrand.
Comply with the Performance Management and Development System (contracting, quarterly reviews and final assessment).
requirements:
Appropriate qualification that allows for registration with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) as Medical Specialist: Anaesthesia.
Registration with the HPCSA as Medical Specialist:
Anaesthesia
At least 3 years appropriate experience in Anaesthesia after registration with HPCSA as a Medical Specialist: Anaesthesia
Management experience, Computer literacy (MS Word, MS Excel, PowerPoint), Experience in administration, finance, education, research and special interest or expertise in a branch of the specialty.
This experience should be in terms of clinical service provision, teaching, administration and research.
Additional recognizable clinical and departmental administration plus qualification/training in Anaesthesia specialties.
A higher degree in the Health Science (Master’s) other than the degree for specialization and experience in the Public Sector will be an advantage.
Sound knowledge of government regulations, policies and acts, the ability to interpreted and implement policies.
Administrative and management knowledge, project management skills, teambuilding, people and interpersonal relations skills, communication skills (verbal and written), organizational, problem-solving and interventional skills.
Highly motivated and enthusiastic to contribute to the anaesthesia care services.
The ability to work under pressure, lead transformational change in a complex environment and the ability to manage change in the department.

responsibilities:

Implement standards, practices, criteria and indicators for quality nursing with the prevention of serious adverse events.
Practice nursing and health care in accordance with the laws and regulations relevant to nursing and health care.
Maintain a constructive working relationship with nursing and other stakeholders.
Participate in the development of protocols and SOPs in the unit.
Demonstrate knowledge on the use of medical equipment and control and repairs of such equipment.
Display leadership and supervisory skills.
Demonstrate decision-making and problem-solving skills.
Effective utilization of material and human resources.
Ability to manage financial and budget allocated to the department.
Display effective conflict and complaint management skills.
Adherence to the Ideal Hospital Realization Framework.
Ability to identify risks and patient safety incidents and manage accordingly.
Compliance to PMDS and CPD requirements.
Ensure a safe and therapeutic environment is created for patients, staff and public.
requirements:

At least 4 years appropriate/recognisable experience in nursing after registration as a Professional Nurse with the SANC in General Nursing.

job_title: Deputy Director: Strategic Planning and Service Delivery
about_role:
The Department of Infrastructure Development (Gauteng) is hiring a Deputy Director: Strategic Planning and Service Delivery in Strategic Planning and Service Delivery, based in Head Office Johannesburg. This is a permanent post, paying R932,292 a year.

How to apply: To apply for the below position, please apply online at https://jobs.gauteng.gov.za. Only online applications will be considered and for general enquiries please contact Human Resource on /.
Reference number to quote: REFS/057431
Closing date: 04 December 2026
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
responsibilities:
Manage the development and review of the Departmental 5-year Strategic Plan and Annual Performance Plan aligned to the environment sector priorities, Government’s Medium-Term Development Plan and Government’s Planning Frameworks.
Manage and coordinate the departmental planning cycle in accordance with applicable planning frameworks, prescripts, timelines and management directives.
Manage and facilitate the consolidation and quality assurance of programme inputs to ensure alignment with departmental priorities, provincial priorities, legislative mandates and national frameworks.
Provide technical and advisory guidance to programme managers on the formulation and refinement of strategic priorities, outputs, indicators and targets.
Manage and facilitate strategic planning sessions, Lekgotlas, APP reviews and related management engagements.
Manage and coordinate the identification of strategic planning gaps, inconsistencies and risks and advise management on appropriate interventions.
Monitor the quality and relevance of strategic planning outputs and recommend improvements to strengthen departmental planning.
Manage the development, review and implementationreadiness of Annual Operational Plans (AOPs) across departmental programmes Coordinate the translation of Strategic Plan and APP commitments into programme-level operational outputs, activities, milestones and deliverables.
Facilitate the assessment of AOP indicators and targets to ensure that they are SMART.
Manage and coordinate the development of Annual Operational Plans (AOP).
Manage and facilitate the development of AOP emanating from strategic outcome and performance outputs in line with the Annual Performance Plan.
Facilitate alignment between AOP commitments, budget allocations, procurement planning and human resource planning inputs.
Facilitate the identification and assessment of implementation, risks, resource constraints and dependencies that may affect planned outputs.
Monitor the integration and consistency of operational plans across programmes and recommend corrective measures where required.
Coordinate the departmental performance reporting cycle and ensure timely consolidation and submission of quarterly and annual performance information.
Manage and coordinate the quality, consistency and integrity of performance information received from departmental programmes.
Manage and coordinate analysis of organizational performance trends, deviations, under-performance and emerging risks and provide management with strategic advice.
Manage the preparation and presentation of consolidated performance reports and management information.
Coordinate the identification of corrective actions and performance improvement measures arising from performance analysis.
Manage and coordinate the development and review of the Department’s Service Delivery Improvement Programme and Plan, Service Delivery Charter and Service Delivery Model.
Provide strategic support to Branches on the development of Service Delivery Improvement Plan, Service Delivery Charter and Service Delivery Mode.
Produce Service Delivery quarterly and annual citizen’s reports as per set departmental, Department of Public Service and Administration and Office of the Premier policies, frameworks and guidelines.
Manage the development and maintenance of required statistical data on programme and service delivery monitoring targets.
Coordinate the assessment of customer satisfaction and ensure that findings are incorporated into service delivery improvement initiatives.
Coordinate the identification and assessment of service delivery challenges, trends and systemic areas requiring improvement.
Manage and coordinate research, environmental scanning and benchmarking activities relating to developments that may impact on departmental service delivery and strategic priorities.
Manage and coordinate the preparation and analysis of environmental scans, SWOT assessments, scenario-planning and strategic research reports.
Facilitate the identification of opportunities for service delivery innovation, process improvement and improved organizational performance.
Coordinate the provision of strategic research and analytical inputs to management planning, performance reviews and decision-making processes.

Build tools that are used across engineering teams, not just a single product.
